# RailOpt AI - real-data model card (DG -> MDU delay)

**REAL data: recorded running times, Sept 2024, Dindigul -> Madurai** (RSTGCN dataset, CC BY-SA 4.0; see docs/DATA_SOURCES.md). Generated by `python -m ml.real_delay` from `metrics_real.json`; do not edit numbers by hand.

The SIMULATED models of Phase 4 (`model_card.md`) were **not trained on real data** and are unchanged. This card only validates whether delay at Madurai can be predicted from what is known when a train leaves Dindigul.

## Conclusion

XGBoost beat the carry-the-DG-delay baseline on test MAE in the main analysis (4.18 vs 4.94 min; difference -0.76 min, 95% CI [-1.53, -0.04]), but not under the train-clustered check [-1.61, +0.18]. The gain is under one minute per train on average. Sensitivity - S1: flagged runs included: XGBoost better; S2: main rows, delays capped at 180 min: Random forest, XGBoost better.

## Design (pre-registered, docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md 57-63)
- Target: arrival delay at MDU (min). Known at DG departure: DG departure and arrival delay, upstream departure delay, train type, terminates_at_MDU, scheduled DG hour (sin/cos), day of week, the train's mean past MDU delay (training dates only, leave-one-out on training rows).
- Split by date: train DG dates <= 2024-09-22, test DG dates > 2024-09-22. Main analysis: 445 train rows, 198 test rows (41 trains; 0 test rows from trains unseen in training).
- 39 runs flagged in the Step 1 audit (MDU exactly on time after DG >= 10 min late; 5 in the test dates) are excluded from the main analysis; S1 includes them.
- Methods, fixed without tuning: B0 carry the DG delay; B1 linear regression; Random forest; XGBoost.
- 95% CIs: percentile bootstrap over test rows (10000 resamples, seed 2024); the MAE difference vs carry is paired. A train-clustered bootstrap (2000 resamples) is shown as a check.

## Limits
- One month, one direction of one corridor, 44 trains; the test set is one week, so the CIs are wide.
- Rows of the same train are correlated; the row bootstrap understates uncertainty (see the clustered CI).
- The flag used to exclude runs is defined from the target; the main analysis therefore removes cases where the carry baseline fails badly. S1 shows the effect.
- The source never records an actual time earlier than scheduled, so early running is invisible.
- Passenger/MEMU and freight trains are not in the data.
